newsitem.title: USA: U.S. court freezes assets of AC Trading.
newsitem.headline: U.S. court freezes assets of AC Trading.

text.p: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission said Tuesday a federal judge froze the assets of AC Trading Group Inc of Napa, California.
U.S. Judge Maxine Chesney of the northern district of California issued an order that also prevents the company from destroying records, the CFTC said.

Last Thursday, the CFTC filed suit claiming that AC Trading, Alexis Carles and Fred Dejong schemed to defraud investors. The CFTC lawsuit claimed that the company told prospective commodity pool investors that AC Trading had been highly profitable, when it actually had at least $1.7 million in trading losses.
The company defrauded investors of more than $300,000, according to the CFTC court documents.
A court hearing was scheduled for Monday in San Francisco on the CFTC's request for an injunction against AC Trading.
